# P-036: complete gap audit of the whole product

Session 2026-11-20 (claude.ai/code session_01YAF6DjRmmukUFojCgZKdEf). Audit only: no product code was changed.
Audited: fenvix-engine-cli `claude/release-1` @ 529c1609 (plus every other branch), fenvix-app `main` @ c59d913 (moved from ce69a6b during the audit when `claude/dashboard-vercel` was merged), fenvix-docs `main` @ 4cc4129, fenvix-landing `main` @ f4d16e3, fenvix-brain-cli `main` @ 1a955a7. Probe workflows: fenvix-engine-cli branch `claude/gap-audit` (runs 44703540913, 44703690223, 44705292795).

Delivered in two places: fenvix-engine-cli branch `claude/gap-audit` (this report, the numbered list `gaps.jsonl`, every agent's findings, notes and matrices under `sessions/2026-11-20-gap-audit/findings/`, and the probe workflows) and fenvix-brain-cli `main` (this report only).

Labels: numbers are MEASURED, ESTIMATED, DECLARED (with source) or UNKNOWN. Each gap says how it is known: RAN (something was executed and showed it), READ (code or config, unambiguous), DOC (only a document or report says so; not verified).

## 0. Summary

The product as it exists today does not keep its promise for most users. Counts below are after deduplication; every
line of sections 2 and 3 has its evidence.

**Wrong results (the worst class), proven by running on release-1:**
- Skip with proof reuses tests whose result changed (Python, MEASURED by re-run): a module on `PYTHONPATH` outside the
  root G-0164, an unowned package in site-packages, a file not in RECORD, `LD_PRELOAD`, `PYTHONWARNINGS`, CPU
  count, umask, `RLIMIT_NOFILE`, host name G-0160 G-0161 G-0162 G-0163. Several are reviewer
  findings (R-008) recorded as fixed: the fix lives in Python code the Rust key no longer uses, and the reviewer tests
  still exercise the dead code (process list).
- `--det-cache` turns a passing order-dependent test into a failure G-0173; `-n N` and `--det-isolate` change
  verdicts silently G-0175 G-0169.
- Node: a test reading the real clock through fake timers is reused G-0122; Go: host name not keyed G-0044,
  a lucky pass of a flaky test frozen G-0046; JVM: the decision is wrong in 8 probes G-0057 G-0059.
- The verifier says "covered / identical" for runs whose time zone, locale, environment, worker/child output, thread
  or I/O order differed, in every language G-0139 G-0180 G-0041 G-0054.
- The hosted service runs a Python-only engine from a stale commit (a20b93d, not on release-1, before the wrong-reuse
  fixes) G-0186; the trial's shadow mode is a label only: tests are skipped for real G-0187; a second job
  overwrites the PR comment with a green tick G-0189.

**Cannot use:**
- Nothing is installable: no package on PyPI or npm (and `detpy` on PyPI is a foreign project G-0170), no
  releases or tags, the engine's default branch is a Block 2 era tip G-0561; artifacts are Linux x86_64 glibc
  ≥ 2.34 only G-0479: not Alpine, Debian 11, Ubuntu 20.04, Amazon Linux 2, macOS, Windows or arm64 (the core does
  not compile on Windows G-0500; on macOS and arm64 the engine builds but the installer and the JVM build
  hard-code Linux x86_64 G-0497 G-0496 G-0478); `pytest --det` crashes on Python 3.9 and 3.10
  G-0556 G-0547.
- No GitHub Action, no MCP server, no API keys or public API G-0215 G-0569; the engine never talks to the
  service: no results, traces, receipts, defects or explorations are sent G-0594; on our machines the customer's
  unchanged `pytest` step runs without the engine.
- Level 1 (asyncio, threads; Block 3 recorded CLOSED) and all L2 browser work are not on release-1 G-0208
  G-0210 G-0214; L2 VM and the syscall backend do not exist.
- `repro`, `explore`, `replay` exist for pytest only and are reachable from no published command; Node, Go and JVM have
  no reproducible-defect workflow, no replay command, no exploration, no culprit, no dependency verdict G-0448
  G-0335 G-0351. Exact culprit and dependency verdict are harness measurements for every language G-0512.
- JVM skip with proof runs every test and can only decide after B has already run G-0353 G-0354; parallel
  under `--det` is absent in Node, Go and JVM G-1044 G-1103; Python `--det-cache=URL` silently writes a local
  directory G-0559.
- Docs site documents another product; landing links into it and sells features that do not exist G-0379.

**Process:** blocks closed on "the prompt's Done means passed" without comparing with the promise, without merging the
work into the release, and with every last review round finding new defects (section 3).

|---|---|---|
| L0 hermetic | order, seeds, virtual clock, fs order, closed network with record/replay (brain ARCHITECTURE.md Levels; engine docs/NODE.md Controls 1-8) | partial: order, Math.random/WebCrypto seeds, Date/performance.now/hrtime, setTimeout/setInterval, readdir/opendir order, TCP/TLS/DNS block + cassette exist (RAN). Missing inside L0: env (G-0126 (ND2-048)), locale (G-0140 (ND2-011)), time zone (G-0139 (ND2-010)), default OS entropy (G-1426 (ND2-021)), UDP (G-0128 (ND2-030)), vm contexts (G-0134 (ND2-023)), workers (G-0152 (ND2-024)), child processes (G-0124 (ND2-062)), fake-timer start time (G-0142 (ND2-026)), record/replay soundness (G-0129 (ND2-036), 037) |
| L1 runtime | 'Node event order later'; sched.ready / sched.timer / sched.io / sched.executor / sched.microtask events in the shared vocabulary (brain ARCHITECTURE.md) | missing: no sched event, no event-loop control or recording (G-0463 (ND2-056), 057, 058, 095); `grep -rn 'sched\.' node/src crates/detpy-node` => nothing |
| L2 deterministic VM | designed: single-core deterministic VM per shard for native threads, whole stack browser + server (brain ARCHITECTURE.md) | missing for Node on release-1 (nothing under node/ or crates/detpy-node; every run prints 'Level 0 active') (G-0464 (ND2-095)) |
| verifier | names the first divergent event; escalates a test L0 does not cover to the next level | partial: `detjs verify` names the first divergent recorded event with a source-mapped site (RAN, TS line correct); it reports 'covered' for tests whose nondeterminism is unrecorded (G-0135 (ND2-001), 010, 023, 024, 048, 057, 062); no escalation exists for Node (no L1) |

## 4. What could not be checked, and why

Twenty audit agents ran in parallel until the user's budget limit (about 09:00 UTC); thirteen were then stopped and
told to flush what they had; three got 20 more minutes for their matrices. What was not checked, by reason:

- **Budget limit (whole areas cut short):** see the PARTIAL line at the top and each agent's "Not covered" list below.
  The prepared scratch projects and venvs are on the audit machine only (they are not committed); a follow-up session
  must re-create them.
- **No network path from the audit machine:** every `*.fenvix.dev` host (docs, console, github App endpoint) answered
  403 through the session proxy, so no live deployment was observed; GitHub Actions artifacts could not be downloaded
  (blob storage refused) and were read through job logs instead; the PyPy image and some downloads were refused.
- **No accounts:** AWS, Supabase, Vercel, Cloudflare, phoenixNAP, the GitHub App registration: nothing could be checked
  in the real accounts (only the code and the infrastructure definitions).
- **Container daemon:** no Docker daemon runs by default on the audit machine. The platform agent started a private one
  for its container probes; the service agents did not, so the Postgres-backed API integration suites ran only against
  a stand-in auth server (APP1) or not at all (APP3, real-API end to end).
- **Other operating systems:** Windows, macOS 15 arm64 and Linux arm64 were probed on GitHub Actions (MEASURED, section
  5); macOS 15 Intel was still running at the cut-off (UNKNOWN); macOS 14 never got a runner.
- **Repository not reachable:** `Mircoguidetti/fenvix-engine` (the older engine) could not be read with this session's
  credentials; `fenvix-infra`, `fenvix-tests` and `fenvix-brain` were not in scope of the prompt and not read.
- **Claims recorded as DOC** (468 lines: from a report or a limits document, not re-verified by running) are listed as
  gaps because the documents themselves say the limit holds; each may be fixed already without the document saying so.


### 4.1 PROC1: process: Blocks 1-3, Node L0, L1 study, cache step 1, market test, head-to-head

#### (a) Could not check

* **jinja mtime leak (P-013 (PROC1-015)) and the more-itertools lock convoy (P-280 (PROC1-016)):** not re-run (would need the
  projects' suites twice under `--det`). Both are DOC: the threads report says they "remain".
* **pytest-dependency** (named with pytest-order by the reviewer): not run. It does not reorder by itself; under
  `--det-seed` a dependent test can run before its dependency and be skipped. Suspected, not proven.
* **Side effects of skipped tests (P-026 (PROC1-135)):** DOC only. The reports call it UNKNOWN; I did not construct a case
  against the carried-set rule of the later rounds.
* **Engine child following and daemons left behind (P-438 (PROC1-154)):** the wait was measured in the market-test harness,
  not in the engine's `follow`; not tested here.
* **ASLR under Docker's default seccomp profile (P-265 (PROC1-068)):** LIMITS R3 says the personality call "fails silently
  under seccomp profiles that forbid it". In this sandbox the header shows `aslr_disabled: true`; I had no container
  with Docker's default profile to confirm the silent failure.
* **Node items** (P-493 (PROC1-076) to -106): read from docs/NODE.md, the Node sources and the reports. I ran no JavaScript
  project; the Node agents own those runs.
* **Side-branch claims** (threads slowdown, coverage on Python < 3.12, exploration cost): read from the reports, not
  re-measured, since the code is not on the audited branch.
* **macOS / Windows:** from docs and CI configuration only.
* **fenvix-app** was searched only for an MCP server and a GitHub Action (none). The PR comment exists in
  `github-app/src/results/render.ts`; its content was not audited here.
* The brain reviewer reports for R-005, R-006, R-007 and R-009 have no saved prompt, so their own "Done means" could
  not be compared with the promise.

## 5. Method and lead verification

Twenty audit agents worked in parallel, one per area, on a common brief (`findings/BRIEF.md`); the lead built every engine artifact of release-1 once (`release/install-image.sh`), ran the platform probes on GitHub Actions, merged the findings, removed cross-agent duplicates (token similarity of the claim ≥ 0.4, the stronger evidence kept, the other cited under `also found by`), and re-ran a sample of the gravest claims. Agents were told never to merge their own similar gaps, so no deduplication was done inside one agent. Input: 2390 product and 783 process entries; after deduplication 2345 and 769. How known (all lines): RAN 1039, READ 1590, DOC 485.

| agent | area |
|---|---|
| PROC1 | process: Blocks 1-3, Node L0, L1 study, cache step 1, market test, head-to-head |
| PROC2 | process: skip with proof lineage (shared cache, audit reruns, Rust port, parallel, culprit, dep verdict, all runners) |
| PROC3 | process: Node cache, other JS runners, Go, JVM, browser/L2, release integration |
| PROC4 | process: GitHub App, dashboard, API, deploy, customer mode, pricing |
| BRANCH | work on branches that did not reach claude/release-1 (engine) or main (app) |
| SWEEP | every limit, TODO, disabled test, CI hole, refusal and pin in engine and app |
| PY1 | Python versions, packaging, first use, runners |
| PY2 | Python pytest-xdist, plugins, concurrency, native code |
| PY3 | Python engine features, matrix, levels |
| ND1 | Node versions, TypeScript toolchains, runners, parallelism, monorepos |
| ND2 | Node controls, features, cache, Bun/Deno, matrix |
| FE | front-end, browser runners, L2 browser lockstep |
| GO | Go |
| JVM | JVM (Java, Kotlin; Gradle, Maven) |
| PLAT | platforms, CI systems, GitHub Action, distribution, MCP, runner wrapper |
| APP1 | service: GitHub App and API |
| APP2 | service: Supabase, infra, deploy, security, billing, operations |
| APP3 | service: dashboard front-end |
| DOCS | documentation site and in-repository docs |
| LAND | landing page |
| LEAD | lead: platform probes on GitHub Actions and re-verification |

### Lead re-verification log

#### Lead re-verification log (claims re-run by the lead on the release-1 wheel, Python 3.13.18, Linux x86_64)

- L-V1 (PY2-001): `--det-cache` makes a passing order-dependent test fail. Project /home/user/audit/work/lead/carry:
  record => `5 passed`; `echo 2 > data.txt`; same command => `reused 4 result(s) with proof, ran 1 ... FAILED
